Abstract A Dedekind domain is the coordinate ring of a nonsingular affine curve. Under that identification every object of 004 - Ideals and Dedekind domains and 005 - Fractional ideals and the ideal class group acquires a geometric name, and the translations are isomorphisms rather than analogies:
Dropping integral closedness - geometrically, allowing the curve to be singular - separates from , and that is the case Track A was in all along: for the order of discriminant Delta,
so Gauss composition is multiplication of ideals, and the two halves of the course are one theory. The arithmetic geometry dictionary Let an irreducible nonsingular affine curve over an algebraically closed
its coordinate ring, so that is a Dedekind domain and is the function field Then every object of the ideal-theoretic chapters has a geometric name, and the correspondence is an isomorphism of groups at each level. Note That is Dedekind exactly when is smooth, and that integral closure is normalization, are proved in Dedekind domains are the smooth affine curves. This note takes that equivalence for granted and pushes it through the rest of the theory.
Fractional ideals as divisors - the isomorphism , and the exponents as valuations
The ideal class group as a divisor class group - the same modulo principal, and where parts from
Invertible fractional ideals are the locally principal ones - the proof under the row invertible Cartier, which is what lets the two Picard groups be one object Fractional ideals as divisors Let
the coordinate ring of a nonsingular affine curve, so that is a Dedekind domain

Unique factorization of ideals into prime over Dedekind Domains says every ideal is with , geometrically, every effective divisor is a non-negative combination of points.
Unique factorization of fractional ideals allows , geometrically, is the free abelian group on the points of , which is how Weil divisors are defined in the first place. So " is free abelian on the primes" (Ideal group) is not analogous to the definition of a Weil divisor: it is that definition, read through the dictionary. The exponent is exactly the discrete valuation at a prime divisor of the geometry course: both are read off the unique factorization in the local ring , a discrete valuation ring. In particular, for ,
so principal fractional ideals correspond to principal divisors and . Containment reverses order : "more divisible" means "smaller ideal", "bigger divisor". In particular
which is the geometric reading of the remark in Fractional ideal that the ideals of are exactly the fractional ideals contained in : ideals are the effective divisors. is a Riemann–Roch space For an ideal with ,
i.e. the inverse fractional ideal is precisely the space of rational functions with poles bounded by , the object whose dimension the Riemann Roch theorem computes (The dimension of a divisor over a curve). " is finitely generated" is the affine shadow of " is finite".
The ideal class group as a divisor class group The ideal class group as a divisor class group
Let the coordinate ring of a nonsingular affine curve, as in Dedekind domain. Then the isomorphism of Fractional ideals as divisors carries onto , hence descends to
the divisor class group of . The two "measures of failure" coincide The ideal class group measures how far is from being a PID; measures how many codimension- subvarieties are not cut out by a single function. Under the dictionary these are literally the same statement, and the examples match:
and the characterization of hypersurfaces used in that example is the statement that height- primes of a UFD are principal (Prime ideals of height 1 are principal at an UFD). Invertibility of ideals in Dedekind domains is the arithmetic form of Correspondence of Weil and Cartier divisors under non singularity assumption:
a Cartier divisor is one that is locally principal; an invertible fractional ideal is one that is locally principal at every prime
the corollary on a nonsingular (or locally factorial) variety says exactly that every Weil divisor is Cartier, i.e. that every fractional ideal is invertible In both proofs the same hypothesis does the work: nonsingularity on one side, integral closedness on the other, deployed through the determinant trick to forbid . Singular curves and non-maximal orders Drop integral closedness, geometrically, allow to be singular, and the correspondence breaks in a precise way: not every ideal is invertible, , and unique factorization into primes fails. This is not a pathology but the situation of the Form class group: for a non-fundamental discriminant the relevant ring is the order , which is not integrally closed. Its class group is defined using only the invertible fractional ideals, the exact analogue of using rather than on a singular curve. See The form class group as a Picard group. Affine versus projective, or: what "removing primes" means For a nonsingular projective curve and an affine open,
Removing points from the curve kills their classes, the geometric counterpart of localizing away from finitely many primes (passing to an -class group). It is also why the affine picture loses the degree map : the degree only survives on the projective model.
Fractional ideals as divisors
The row of the dictionary reading invertible fractional ideal Cartier divisor is a theorem, and it is what makes the Picard group of a ring and the Picard group of a variety one object rather than two homonyms.Localization at a prime ideal Let

is a local ring, its unique maximal ideal being , and its units are the with localization preserves sums, products and inclusions of submodules, and for finitely generated it commutes with the inverse:
an ideal is the whole ring iff for every maximal ; equivalently iff for some maximal , and then Note This is the minimum needed to state what locally principal means, and to run Invertible fractional ideals are the locally principal ones. Point is the standard "a proper ideal is contained in a maximal one" plus the observation that a unit cannot be pushed into ; point is where finite generation is spent, an infinite intersection not commuting with localization in general.

The missing proof under a dictionary row The arithmetic geometry dictionary lists "invertible fractional ideal" against "Cartier divisor, i.e. locally principal" as a translation. This theorem is what makes that row a theorem rather than a pun, and with it the two definitions of the Picard group, the arithmetic one and the geometric one, become the same group entry by entry. Adding Cartier divisors multiplies their local equations, which is exactly multiplication of ideals read locally: that is why the two group laws agree. What this explains about the hypotheses on both sides
The geometric note carries a nonsingularity hypothesis it does not need. Cartier divisor assumes nonsingular in codimension , but the Cartier definition never uses it: it is needed only to compare with Weil divisors. The arithmetic likewise needs no smoothness, only Noetherianity. That is precisely why both survive on , which is singular, while and unique factorization do not.
The two corollaries are twins. of Correspondence of Weil and Cartier divisors under non singularity assumption is the geometric form of Invertibility of ideals in Dedekind domains: nonsingularity on one side, integral closedness on the other, both saying every divisor is locally principal. A third description exists, isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves under , with ; it is where the name comes from. The vault has no sheaves, so it is mentioned and not pursued.
The ring this happens in, the order of discriminant Delta, and the normalized norm form attaching an ideal to a form are already in 003 - The form class group, where Gauss composition needed them; the maximal order case, with the narrow class group, is 007 - The narrow class group and the form class group. What is left is the isomorphism itself, for an arbitrary order.The form class group as a Picard group Let
a discriminant, , not a square
the quadratic order of discriminant Delta, generated by
a primitive binary quadratic form of discriminant , and the norm of , with Then, setting the assignment is such that the norm form of the ideal is the form itself, once divided by the index: in the ordered basis of , and for ,
which is the normalized norm form - where this ideal, the factor and the division by it all come from it induces a group isomorphism under which
proper equivalence becomes equality of ideal classes
the Dirichlet composition computes the product of ideals , which is by definition the Gauss composition - so the map is a homomorphism for free, and the content of this point is that the closed formula agrees with it, by Gauss composition is well defined on classes
the principal form becomes the class of itself the inverse becomes the conjugate ideal Where the ideal comes from
The construction. The ideal , the expansion out of , the index and the reason the division by it is forced rather than chosen are all Realizing a quadratic form as a norm form. Only the principal class consists of norm forms on the nose; every other class is reached through the substitution , and the normalization is its determinant.
At the principal form. Read at this gives and , hence : the generator of the Quadratic order is nothing but at the principal form, which is point .
Where the group law comes from. Multiplicativity of the norm, applied to that normalized expression, is what becomes the composition of forms, and this is the identity of Dirichlet composition is a direct composition read on ideals. The ordered basis, not the ideal, carries the sign The sign of . , so and are the same ideal, but the second ordered basis returns . Flipping the orientation of the basis conjugates the form, which is exactly why is the class of in point , and why the correspondence needs an ordered basis to be a bijection on the nose rather than up to inversion.
The conjugate generator. is a different matter: it gives the same norm form , in a positively oriented basis, but generates the conjugate ideal. That is the convention of Gauss composition is well defined on classes, and the two differ by inversion. Why the whole composition theory was needed
On the ideal side the group axioms are free, multiplication of ideals being obviously commutative, associative and unital. Everything painful in The form class group is an abelian group, the congruence system of Common middle coefficient of two united forms, the CRT argument for associativity, the unitedness hypothesis, is the cost of writing that product down in coordinates, in terms of the -basis rather than intrinsically.
What the coordinates were hiding. , the common middle coefficient, is the coordinate of the generator of ; " united" is the condition that does not obstruct writing that generator. By the conductor description of the order, is integrally closed only for fundamental, so for conductor it is not a Dedekind domain and not all of its fractional ideals are invertible. The ideals coming from primitive forms are exactly the invertible ones. Geometrically this is the singular-curve situation: is a singular arithmetic curve, its normalization is , and . So the form class group is a Picard group of a singular curve, and primitivity of a form is the arithmetic name for invertibility of the corresponding sheaf. Composition and the chord–tangent law are the same kind of object Both the Dirichlet composition and the group law on a plane cubic are explicit polynomial formulas realizing an abstract class-group law: In both cases the definition of the group is a quotient of divisors (or ideals) by principal ones, and the content of the theorem is that the operation can be computed by bilinear algebra in coordinates. The bilinear substitutions of Composition of binary quadratic forms play exactly the role of the rational addition formulas . Where the analogy stops A conic of discriminant is a genus- curve, so its own is trivial: the group is not the geometry of one conic, but of the family of all classes at once, i.e. of the arithmetic curve . The finiteness of (the class number) has no counterpart for of a curve over an algebraically closed field, where the class group is the Picard variety, a positive-dimensional abelian variety rather than a finite group.

The group is already built, out of Dirichlet composition and the four lemmas repairing it, and The form class group is an abelian group is already proved with no ring theory at all. What this note adds is a description of that same law which makes no choice of coordinates, and the generalization below. Warning
Which half is the definition. The ideal expression is one outright: the product of ideals is canonical, and depends only on because proper equivalence is a change of oriented -basis, so nothing has to be checked. Gauss's own is not a definition as it stands: nothing says such an exists, nor that is independent of the two choices made, the representatives and the substitution.
The price is an orientation convention. Reversing the basis of conjugates the form, , hence inverts the class, which is why "positively oriented" cannot be dropped. The subtlety does not disappear, it moves from the substitution to the basis, and directness is what picks the same orientation on the form side.
So the theorem is a comparison, not a repair. Gauss composition is well defined on classes says every direct composition of arbitrary representatives lands in the class of the product ideal, which buys existence and independence for Gauss's description in one stroke. Idea This is composition read one level up, on classes instead of on forms, and it is the operation Gauss defines in the Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), Section V, from Art. 234 onward. It chooses no coordinates, no common middle coefficient and no representatives, and its commutativity is a symmetry of the definition rather than a computation. The price is that it is not a formula: nothing here computes . Dirichlet composition is the formula, and the two are the same operation, which is point of the theorem. Read backwards, that turns the whole of 002 into an algorithm for a law that was already there. Where "multiplication of ideals" is made good on Three things are asserted here and paid for later. hermite-problem-for-multidimensional-con.title: Hermite problem for multidimensional continued fractions
hermite-problem-for-multidimensional-con.description:
Let be a real algebraic number of degree greater than . Then Hermite's problem asks for an extension of continued-fraction methods in which algebraic numbers are characterized by suitable periodic expansions, extending Euler-Lagrange theorem for continued fractions. Note
Historical motivation. Jacobi's two-dimensional algorithm was designed to address cubic irrationalities; Perron's generalization allows more coordinates. Scope. “Multidimensional continued fraction” is not one universal algorithm. A periodicity theorem must specify its update, admissibility, convergence, and the meaning of the encoded number.
Research context. The classical periodic-characterization problem is discussed as unresolved in Accossato–Murru–Romeo, introduction and §7. Let a periodic projective algorithm have period matrix ; satisfy ; the eigenvalue have a one-dimensional eigenspace. Then every is algebraic over . The characteristic equation makes algebraic. Solving over gives a basis vector for its one-dimensional kernel; normalizing its last coordinate to puts all in . Warning This is the matrix mechanism behind the periodic-to-algebraic direction. Without a condition on the eigenspace, a rational matrix can fix transcendental coordinate ratios; the identity matrix is an immediate example.

The missing proof under a dictionary row The arithmetic geometry dictionary lists "invertible fractional ideal" against "Cartier divisor, i.e. locally principal" as a translation. This theorem is what makes that row a theorem rather than a pun, and with it the two definitions of the Picard group, the arithmetic one and the geometric one, become the same group entry by entry. Adding Cartier divisors multiplies their local equations, which is exactly multiplication of ideals read locally: that is why the two group laws agree. What this explains about the hypotheses on both sides
The geometric note carries a nonsingularity hypothesis it does not need. Cartier divisor assumes nonsingular in codimension , but the Cartier definition never uses it: it is needed only to compare with Weil divisors. The arithmetic likewise needs no smoothness, only Noetherianity. That is precisely why both survive on , which is singular, while and unique factorization do not.
The two corollaries are twins. of Correspondence of Weil and Cartier divisors under non singularity assumption is the geometric form of Invertibility of ideals in Dedekind domains: nonsingularity on one side, integral closedness on the other, both saying every divisor is locally principal. A third description exists, isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves under , with ; it is where the name comes from. The vault has no sheaves, so it is mentioned and not pursued.

quadratic-sieve.html.title: Quadratic sieve
quadratic-sieve.html.description:
Let an odd nonsquare integer to factor for integers in a finite interval near a smoothness bound Then the quadratic sieve seeks square relations by the following procedure. Trial-divide by primes at most . If one is a proper divisor, return it. Otherwise take the factor base consisting of and odd primes for which is a nonzero quadratic residue modulo . Initialize a residual value for every in the interval, recording the sign of .
For each factor-base prime , find every root of (one generally uses Tonelli-Shanks algorithm). Visit the positions and divide repeatedly by , recording the exponent. Retain precisely the positions with residual value . Their values are smooth over the factor base.
Find a nonzero dependency among the signed parity vectors by Square products from parity vectors. For its selected set define Then . Test and . Return a proper factor, or try another dependency or collect more relations. Idea A prime divides on arithmetic progressions. Sieve those progressions instead of trial-dividing each value independently.
For , the condition is exactly . For odd use the Legendre symbol to test existence and Tonelli-Shanks square root algorithm to find the roots. Modulo , an odd has the root . Every relevant prime power is completely removed by repeated division. The residual equals exactly when no other prime factor remains. An even sign coordinate and even prime exponents make the product an integer square; reducing each proves the congruence.
The output is certified by its gcd, as in Factoring from a congruence of squares. Warning Repeated powers. Dividing just once at each visited position loses multiplicities and can incorrectly reject smooth values. Scope. These steps establish correctness of accepted relations and factors, not a bound on how many smooth values the chosen interval contains.

Find the roots when building the base. In point , for each prime , find the distinct roots of and store the corresponding . This is polynomial root finding over : for small , one can test every residue. More generally, is the product of the distinct linear factors of . Compute by repeated squaring, then split into linear factors using Cantor-Zassenhaus for odd ; for , test . Each factor supplies a root. These roots are computed once when constructing and reused throughout the sieve. Use the roots to visit candidate pairs. For each stored and each fixed , put and visit the arithmetic progression , , restricted to and the eligible positions in the code. Thus the congruence is implemented by jumps of size , without testing it separately at every position. At each visited pair, divide all powers of out of the norm residual , recording the exponent in .
Why the root identifies the algebraic factor. For a primitive pair, if then : monicity would otherwise give . Hence the unique possible root is . The sieve uses this identity in reverse, starting from to locate . By Prime support of primitive linear algebraic integers, the entire exponent of in the norm belongs to this , even if is a repeated root of .
Combine both sieves to certify smoothness. The rational sieve similarly visits and removes all powers of from . A single progression only certifies divisibility by one prime. After processing all base primes, retain exactly the pairs with : both original values then factor completely over the bases, with the exponents already recorded. Reject any other pair without factoring its leftover residual. This is the same principle as the Quadratic sieve, applied to two linked values. These define the two bases and the relations to be collected.
By Prime support of primitive linear algebraic integers, every contributing prime has degree one, and its rational prime divides the norm. Conversely every prime factor of the norm gives a contributing degree-one prime. Thus the bounds on the two supports agree. Idea Rational sieve. For fixed , a prime divides on the progression . Algebraic sieve. A prime contains on the progression . At primitive pairs, its multiplicity is the corresponding exponent in .
Complete removal. Divide residual absolute values by all powers of each relevant prime, as in Quadratic sieve. Residual certifies smoothness. Warning Signs. The rational product must be positive as well as have even exponents. The absolute algebraic norm is used only to test support; its smoothness does not certify that the algebraic element is a square. The ideals coming from primitive forms are exactly the invertible ones. Geometrically this is the singular-curve situation: is a singular arithmetic curve, its normalization is , and . Where the analogy stops A conic of discriminant is a genus- curve, so its own is trivial: the group is not the geometry of one conic, but of the family of all classes at once, i.e. of the arithmetic curve . The finiteness of (the class number) has no counterpart for of a curve over an algebraically closed field, where the class group is the Picard variety, a positive-dimensional abelian variety rather than a finite group.

Let the coordinate ring of a nonsingular affine curve, as in Dedekind domain. Then the isomorphism of Fractional ideals as divisors carries onto , hence descends to
the divisor class group of . The two "measures of failure" coincide The ideal class group measures how far is from being a PID; measures how many codimension- subvarieties are not cut out by a single function. Under the dictionary these are literally the same statement, and the examples match:
and the characterization of hypersurfaces used in that example is the statement that height- primes of a UFD are principal (Prime ideals of height 1 are principal at an UFD). Invertibility of ideals in Dedekind domains is the arithmetic form of Correspondence of Weil and Cartier divisors under non singularity assumption:
a Cartier divisor is one that is locally principal; an invertible fractional ideal is one that is locally principal at every prime
the corollary on a nonsingular (or locally factorial) variety says exactly that every Weil divisor is Cartier, i.e. that every fractional ideal is invertible In both proofs the same hypothesis does the work: nonsingularity on one side, integral closedness on the other, deployed through the determinant trick to forbid . Singular curves and non-maximal orders Drop integral closedness, geometrically, allow to be singular, and the correspondence breaks in a precise way: not every ideal is invertible, , and unique factorization into primes fails. This is not a pathology but the situation of the Form class group: for a non-fundamental discriminant the relevant ring is the order , which is not integrally closed. Its class group is defined using only the invertible fractional ideals, the exact analogue of using rather than on a singular curve. See The form class group as a Picard group. Affine versus projective, or: what "removing primes" means For a nonsingular projective curve and an affine open,
Removing points from the curve kills their classes, the geometric counterpart of localizing away from finitely many primes (passing to an -class group). It is also why the affine picture loses the degree map : the degree only survives on the projective model.

a Fractional ideal of Then can be uniquely factored as a product of integral powers of prime ideals of , with prime and not necessarily positive. Existence. Let generate . Since they lie in , write with , . Setting ,
so is an ideal of . By Unique factorization of ideals into prime over Dedekind Domains, and
so by invertibility (Invertibility of ideals in Dedekind domains) Uniqueness. Assume , all distinct and likewise all . Since multiplying a fractional ideal by changes nothing, clearing the negative exponents gives
Both sides are ideals of , so the result follows from the uniqueness part of Unique factorization of ideals into prime over Dedekind Domains. Important Allowing negative exponents is exactly what turns the multiplicative monoid of ideals into a group: this theorem says is free abelian on the prime ideals. See Ideal group. unique-factorization-of-ideals-into-prim.title: Unique factorization of ideals into prime over Dedekind Domains
unique-factorization-of-ideals-into-prim.description:
Let a Dedekind domain with field of fractions
a non-zero ideal Then can be uniquely factored as a product of prime ideals of . Existence. Suppose some non-zero ideal of cannot be written as a product of prime ideals. Since is Noetherian we may take maximal with respect to this property. Then is not prime, hence properly contained in some prime ideal of .
Since , is contained in and contains . By the proof of Invertibility of ideals in Dedekind domains, properly contains , and therefore cannot be contained in : otherwise the elements of would be integral over by Characterization of integral elements via finitely generated modules, contradicting integral closedness. Hence , so by maximality of we can write with prime. Multiplying by and using invertibility, contradicting the choice of . Uniqueness. Suppose with all factors prime. Then and since is prime, for some . By maximality of (axiom (ii)), . WLOG ; cancel using invertibility and iterate. The process cannot terminate with for a non-empty set of factors, since that would put inside a prime ideal. Important
Unique factorization is repaired at the level of ideals. This is the theorem that repairs the failure of element-wise unique factorization in : elements need not factor uniquely, but the ideals they generate always do. The extent of the discrepancy is measured by the ideal class group , which is trivial exactly when is a PID.
The converse holds, so this is a characterization. A domain in which every non-zero ideal is some product of primes is already Dedekind (Domains whose ideals factor into primes are Dedekind): the mere existence of a factorization forces the three axioms, and uniqueness then comes for free. So the hypotheses are not an ad hoc list, they are exactly equivalent to the conclusion.

united-forms.html.title: United forms
united-forms.html.description:
Let and binary quadratic forms of the same discriminant Then and are united if
Note because (Discriminant of an integral quadratic form), so the condition makes sense. Idea "United" is precisely the coprimality hypothesis needed to solve the system of simultaneous congruences that produces the common middle coefficient , see Common middle coefficient of two united forms. Without it the Dirichlet composition cannot even be written down. Important Being united is not a condition on classes but on representatives. It is never an obstruction, because every class contains a representative united with any prescribed form, which is exactly what makes the composition well defined on .
What the coprimality is really for Later in the course the condition acquires a one line meaning. Composing amounts to multiplying the ideals and of the order of discriminant Delta, with the common generator, and the product contains , and for free. What is not free is itself, and it lies in the product precisely when Bezout applies, i.e. when :
So united is the condition for the product ideal to have a generator one can write down, which is why without it the Dirichlet composition has no formula and why the obstruction is a property of representatives rather than of classes. The computation is The product of the ideals of two concordant forms; the version with replaced by the weaker gcd above is what Common middle coefficient of two united forms extracts from it.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.

info_allowResizing.description: Whether or not to allow the sidebars to be resized

info_allowCollapsing.description: Whether or not to allow the sidebars to be collapsed

info_rightDefaultWidth.description: The default width of the right sidebar

info_leftDefaultWidth.description: The default width of the left sidebar

info_selector.description: CSS selector for an element. The feature will be placed relative to this element.

info_type.description: Will this feature be placed before, after, or inside (at the beggining or end).

info_featurePlacement.description: Where to place this feature on the page. (Relative to the selector)

info_sourcePath.description: The local path to the source .html file which will be included.

info_allowFoldingLists.description: Whether or not to allow lists to be folded

info_allowFoldingHeadings.description: Whether or not to allow headings to be folded

info_siteUrl.description: The url that this site will be hosted at

info_authorName.description: The name of the author of the site
